title: Upgrading a packaging line
text:
A food manufacturer is upgrading one of its packaging lines. Two vendors work side by side. The first installs the new machines to a fixed plan. The second configures the control software in two-week iterations.

The machine crew complains that the software crew keeps changing the line's settings during the night shift. Both crews have stopped using the project's agreed rule that every change to the line is logged on the shared board. The plant manager wants the line running again in six weeks.

title: Replacing a city's parking permits
text:
A city council is replacing paper parking permits with a mobile app and number-plate cameras. The transport director sponsors the project and wants it live before the summer. The team builds the app in two-week iterations; a contractor installs the cameras to a fixed plan.

The residents' association says the cameras invade privacy and has started a petition against the project. Local shop owners have not taken a position, and the team judges that neutral is all it needs from them. The council's data protection officer has not yet heard of the project, although the cameras will store number-plate data.

title: A loyalty app for a retail chain
text:
A retail chain is building a customer loyalty app in two-week sprints; the first release is due in three months.

The marketing department expects the app to collect detailed shopping data for its campaigns. The store operations department expects checkout to stay as fast as today, with no extra steps for cashiers. In early user tests, many shoppers gave up on signing up when the app asked for a lot of personal information.

title: Automating a warehouse
text:
A logistics company is automating one of its warehouses. A construction contractor will install robots, racking and conveyors, and the building must pass a fire-safety inspection before it can open.

The software that routes orders to the robots is new to the company. The operations team is still discovering what it will need from the software, and expects to learn a lot from early trials. The board wants the warehouse operating in 12 months.
